title: State-resolved quantum-information fingerprints of partial dynamical symmetry in the interacting boson model
summary: Partial dynamical symmetry (PDS) is an algebraic structure in which a symmetry is neither exact nor fully broken: a subset of eigenstates keeps good quantum numbers and stays solvable while the rest mix. It is currently identified from spectroscopy. We ask whether it also leaves a purely structural mark in the eigenstates, and find, for the $sd$-IBM Hamiltonians studied here, that it does, though not in the magnitude of entanglement.
